notes: A clearer queue, honest wait times and a steadier window. Cluster has a new Queue section: one queue per partition, in the order Slurm tries the jobs, with what each job asks for (CPUs, RAM per computer, GPUs, computers, time limit), the login that Slurm shows for its owner, how long it has waited and what the jobs ahead of it ask for in all. Jobs that wait for something other than room (held, waiting for another job, scheduled for later, stopped by a limit, unable to start as asked) are folded apart by reason, with what each reason means, and a wait of two weeks in line is flagged. Your own jobs are in bold and listed on top with a button that finds each one in its queue; there is also "Only my jobs" and a search, and a waiting job in Jobs has "See the whole queue". A waiting job no longer leads with Slurm's planned start, which proved far too pessimistic: it says first whether there is room for it right now, and shows Slurm's plan as a cautious one. The "nodes could start this right now" line and "When would it start?" now take into account the memory that running jobs already hold, say what is missing, and explain why every variation shows the same time. The window is steadier: if it ever stops answering the app records where it was stuck, an unexpected error is shown once instead of piling up dialogs, the window repaints itself after a Remote Desktop or display change, and the Jobs "Table" view, the Files "Details" view and the Queue no longer freeze for seconds when they refresh a hundred or more rows. Checked against simulated Slurm output and very large simulated queues, not yet on the real Draco: if a panel looks wrong or empty, please tell us. Not code-signed yet.
